Niva Bupa Health Insurance, one of India’s leading standalone health insurers, is set to host the Niva Bupa Walk for Healthy Cities in New Delhi. Tennis icon and Olympic medallist Sania Mirza is coming to the capital this Sunday, September 27, to lead the Niva Bupa Walk for Healthy Cities, an initiative that brings together fitness, community and environmental action.The initiative aims to bring together citizens, fitness enthusiasts, families, corporate employees and community groups for a morning centred on walking, fitness and community engagement. Through the Niva Bupa Walk for Healthy Cities, we want to make healthy living more participative, engaging and relevant to everyday life. Having Sania Mirza lead this initiative in Delhi adds an incredible energy to the movement and we hope her presence inspires more people to step out, move together and take small but meaningful steps towards healthier lives and healthier cities. ”The initiative brings together three simple ideas, move for your health, connect with your community and act for your environment, reinforcing the belief that small actions, when taken collectively, can create a larger impact.
Article Summary: Tennis icon and Olympic medallist Sania Mirza is coming to the capital this Sunday, September 27, to lead the Niva Bupa Walk for Healthy Cities. Article Title: 'Dubai-based scammers looted Rs 94,000 crore': CBI arrests Mahadev app key accused deported from UAE
Article Text:
Abhishek Kumar coordinated various panels in the Mahadev network

NEW DELHI:

CBI on Thursday arrested Abhishek Kumar, a key accused in the Mahadev online betting and gambling case in which Enforcement Directorate (ED) has claimed that the perpetrators of the illegal activities have so far generated and laundered proceeds of crime of more than Rs 94,000 crore.Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI immediately after he arrived at Hyderabad airport from Dubai. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni - both continue to operate the gambling network from the UAE and other jurisdictions.Kumar coordinated various panels in the Mahadev network and was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime, a CBI spokesperson said. He has been taken to Raipur and produced before a special court for police remand. So far, seven Red Corner Notices and two extradition requests have been pending against other accused.The Mahadev online betting and gambling app is still active and proceeds of crime of Rs 94,000 crore have been generated so far by the accused, who are in Dubai, ED has said in its latest chargesheet in the case. More than Rs 1,000 crore has been invested in Indian share markets through foreign portfolio investments (FPIs), the agency said.It estimated that in the last few years, the accused generated more than Rs 11,000 crore annually from illegal online gambling and betting activities.Based on analysis of various seized digital evidence and statements of several accused, ED said that "it can be estimated that proceeds of crime worth Rs 11,400 crore (approx) must have been generated by illegal operations of Mahadev online book every year". The gambling network has been running since 2019."As per latest findings, Mahadev app is still running a huge number of panels. Estimated proceeds of crime generated by the app is around Rs 75,000-80,000 crore during the last seven years," ED has said. In addition, it said other illegal apps run by the syndicate like Skyexchange.com and Lotus365.com have generated proceeds of crime of over Rs 14,000 crore."A majority of the proceeds of crime was layered and transferred to the promoters based in Dubai," ED stated.The agency has so far attached assets worth over Rs 2,000 crore linked to various accused. The agency said the above estimation of proceeds of crime is only a provisional figure and is likely to go up.
Article Summary: Abhishek Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni. Kumar was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime.

NEW DELHI: Meeting on the margins of United Nations General Assembly, G4 countries called for a reform of the UNSC at the earliest, saying in a joint statement that the council is currently unable to effectively discharge its core responsibility of maintaining international peace and security.The G4 group of countries (India, Japan, Brazil, and Germany) supports urgent reforms of the security council through the expansion in both permanent and non-permanent categories of membership of UNSC."Discussed the imperative of reformed multilateralism and a more representative, responsive and effective UN Security Council that reflects today's global realities. Article Title: Wangchuk fears 'encounter' after accusing govt of Ladakh atrocities
Article Text:
Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk

SRINAGAR

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said Thursday he feared he could be subjected to an “encounter” for speaking out against what he called atrocities in Ladakh, a year after police firing killed four protesters in Leh.Drawing a comparison with Tibet, Wangchuk said Ladakhis had chosen India because of its democracy. “Today, such atrocities are being committed in Ladakh that even China is not doing in Tibet. That is what you are seeing today,” he said, addressing a gathering on the first anniversary of the police firing on Sept 24, 2025.He sought a people’s tribunal to probe the killings, saying a judicial commission set up by Union home ministry had yet to submit its report.“Last year on this day, four people died... Bullets hit their chests, backs, and heads. Those were not pellets that would merely injure you or hurt your eyes. Bullets were fired indiscriminately from automatic weapons, like AK-47s, at the unarmed youth of Ladakh who were peacefully demanding their rights,” Wangchuk alleged.He rejected claims that the protests were triggered by him. He alleged that before the 2020 LAHDC-Leh elections, Ladakhi representatives opposed to holding polls were taken to New Delhi on a special flight and promised statehood and Sixth Schedule status.He blamed “govt failure to honour those promises” for last year’s demonstrations.Authorities imposed curfew-like restrictions in Leh after the alleged “arson and rioting” and subsequent police firing. FIRs were filed and 81 people arrested, including Wangchuk. He was charged under NSA and sent to Jodhpur jail. After 170 days, Union govt withdrew his detention on March 14 this year and he was set free.He feared further action, saying: “They sent me to jail. Inquiries have been made against me. Only an encounter is left. I am ready for that. It is my last wish. Experts tell me that you will be subjected to an encounter. So be it. Let the country wake up, this is my hope.”A complete shutdown was observed in Leh on Thursday, designated as Martyr’s Day. Wangchuk accused authorities of stopping people from attending the rally, a claim denied by police.Police said Ladakh Buddhist Association had sought permission for a public meeting at Leh’s NDS stadium, which has a capacity of 10,000. The administration granted permission for a prayer meet from 10am to noon. Police reported a turnout of 800 at the event and denied allegations that they erected barricades to stop people from reaching the venue.
Article Summary: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said he feared he could be subjected to an ‘encounter’ for speaking out against what he called atrocities in Ladakh. He sought a people’s tribunal to probe the killings, saying a judicial commission set up by Union home ministry had yet to submit report.

Article Title: Centre pleads for prospective effect of SC creamy layer ruling
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Facing the task of implementing Supreme Court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation from the retrospective date of 2012, Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it.The court had in March held that the income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine the creamy layer of a candidate for exclusion from OBC reservation, and status and category of a parent's job had to be considered with an 'income/wealth test' as an additional criterion. It made the verdict implementable from 2012, when the case was first filed.In a written note filed by additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, govt submitted that the retrospective application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the time and create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression."The retrospective implementation of the present judgement would create changes in candidates' service and cadre allocation... as it would affect the services of persons appointed on the basis of CSE-2012 onward and cause a cascading effect among civil servants... The aforementioned cascading effect will impact not only OBC candidates but also reverberate across all categories including (unreserved category) of the civil services," the note said.Govt said a reasonable time of two years should be given to it to undertake the necessary exercise of establishing equivalence of posts, after consulting all the stakeholders and formulating a uniform policy/mechanism for determination of OBC creamy layer status."Union of India is only praying for a limited deferral of the operationalisation of the law laid down by this hon'ble court for a period of two years so that the competing rights can be adjusted consistent with the administrative contingencies and an effective equivalence exercise is carried out," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme Court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation from retrospective date of 2012. Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it. Court had in March held that the income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine the creamy layer of a candidate for exclusion.

Article Title: NALSAR students screen Umar Khalid documentary after screenings cancelled at IIIT-Hyderabad, NLSIU
Article Text:
The screening was a private event restricted to students.

Prisoner No. 626710 is Present

Prisoner No. 626710 is Present





Hyderabad: The screening of Umar Khalid’s documentary,, which was cancelled at the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad (IIIT-H), and National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, was held at NALSAR University of Law in the city on Wednesday evening. A group of students who independently organised the “solidarity screening” said it was held to offer an opportunity “to engage directly with the film’s questions about rights, accountability and the human cost of prolonged incarceration, while expressing solidarity with those affected by these failures of the justice system”.The screening was a private event restricted to students.“The film raises urgent concerns about the delay in the justice system, and about undertrial prisoners being kept in custody for years without their trials even beginning,” one of the students told TOI via email. “When a person remains imprisoned for six years without trial, the delay itself becomes a serious denial of justice. Law cannot, and should not, be used as a tool of violence without convictions. The process cannot become the punishment,” the email added.NALSAR students have called on student bodies across universities to organise similar screenings of the documentary.The documentary has not been certified by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC).The board has stated that screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been obtained.Last week, the screening at IIIT-H was cancelled after the CBFC flagged the issue on X. The institute later said that the proposed event had not been organised or authorised by its management. At NLSIU, too, the event, which was initially postponed, was later cancelled after organisers said they faced threats of criminal action, intimidation, doxxing and other forms of harassment., directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, is a documentary about Khalid, tracing his journey from student activist to his arrest in 2020 and subsequent incarceration.Meanwhile, NALSAR vice-chancellor, Prof Srikrishna Deva Rao, said, “NALSAR University of Law did not authorise screening of the documentary film Prisoner No 626710 on its campus. No official permission for the same was given to anybody by any University authority,”
Article Summary: The screening was a private event restricted to students. NALSAR students have called on student bodies across universities to organise similar screenings. The documentary has not been certified by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) The board has stated that screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been obtained.

NEW DELHI: National Board of Examinations in Medical Sciences (NBEMS) Thursday declared NEET-PG 2026 result, with 2,65,960 candidates having appeared in the exam held in two phases this year. Article Title: Tarun Tejpal challenges rape conviction, SC seeks Goa govt response
Article Text:
Tejpal surrendered before a Goa court on September 14

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has issued notice to the Goa government on a plea filed by former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal challenging the Bombay high court judgment convicting him in a 2013 sexual assault case and sentencing him to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment.The bench sought the state’s response on Tejpal’s challenge to the August 6 High Court verdict, which overturned his acquittal by a trial court in May 2021. The high court had convicted him of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in Goa in November 2013 and also imposed a fine of more than Rs 10 lakh, to be paid to the survivor.Tejpal surrendered before a Goa court on September 14 after the Supreme Court directed him to do so within three weeks. He was subsequently sent to Central Jail at Colvale in North Goa to serve his sentence.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has issued notice to the Goa government on a plea filed by former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal. He was convicted of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in Goa in November 2013 and also imposed a fine of more than Rs 10 lakh, to be paid to the survivor.

Article Title: 6 Ukrainians accused of training armed rebels in India, Myanmar get default bail

NEW DELHI: An NIA court in Delhi Wednesday granted bail to six Ukrainian nationals arrested in March this year for allegedly running a training camp for ethnic armed rebels in India and Myanmar.The court, which ordered their release on a cash bond of Rs 1 lakh each, also discharged them from offences under the Immigration and Foreigners Act following after the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), which deals with the immigration matters involving foreign nationals, settled the offences on payment of a penalty of Rs 5.5 lakh each.The offences, which pertained to illegal entry and visa violations, are compoundable at the level of the FRRO.Special judge Prashant Sharma granted them default bail on grounds of parity with their American co-accused Matthew Aaron Van Dyke.While granting bail to Dyke on Sept 18, the judge had dismissed the NIA’s opposition, observing that even if the probe was far from over, “at this stage it cannot be concluded that applicant/ accused Matthew Aaron Vandyke is not entitled for default bail”.Default bail is provisioned in the UAPA if the probe agency doesn’t file charge sheet containing offences under the anti-terror law with 180 days of arresting the accused. Following this, the court had directed that the other six accused could also seek default bail.Earlier this month, the agency filed a charge sheet which did not mention provisions of the UAPA, 1967, which was invoked in the initial FIR.
Article Summary: Six Ukrainian nationals arrested in March this year for allegedly running a training camp for ethnic armed rebels in India and Myanmar. The court discharged them from offences under the Immigration and Foreigners Act. The Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO) settled the offences on payment of a penalty of Rs 5.5 lakh each.

Article Title: Food warnings must drive reformulation, says ex-FSSAI chief
Article Text:
94% of packaged foods may face warnings under nutrient limits; FSSAI ex-chief Pawan Kumar Agarwal urges SC for phased food warning rollout

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: A day after FSSAI filed its compliance affidavit on front-of-pack warning labels, former FSSAI CEO Pawan Kumar Agarwal said he was comfortable with the regulator’s position, provided the transition period leads to significant improvement in the nutritional composition of packaged foods.Agarwal, through the Food Future Foundation, filed an intervention application in the Supreme Court on September 22 in the ongoing case on front-of-pack warning labels. The application seeks to assist the court on the questions it had raised on the design, scientific basis and implementation of the proposed warning system.The intervention says the transition period should drive progressive reformulation, not merely allow companies to change packaging. It proposes interim nutrient thresholds, followed by tighter limits over three to five years, with milestones and timelines announced upfront.It also recommends that any one nutrient crossing the prescribed threshold should trigger a warning, so a beverage high in sugar, for instance, cannot escape a warning because it remains below the sodium and saturated fat limits.The intervention cites a NatFirst analysis of 44,109 barcode records of packaged, branded food products available at retail in India.It found that 94.1% of the records exceeded at least one nutrient threshold, while 85.3% of those classified as high in fat, sugar and salt exceeded two or more thresholds.The figures are not weighted by sales or consumption, and NatFirst said they do not establish that individual products are unsafe, unhealthy or non-compliant. The Foundation has also proposed product-level modelling to set interim thresholds and assess their impact on warnings and reformulation.FSSAI’s September 23 affidavit proposes a single-phase rollout, with about four months to finalise the regulations, followed by a 60-day stakeholder and World Trade Organization consultation and a 365-day implementation period for food businesses. It has a red hexagon on a white square. One nutrient crossing the threshold would be named in the hexagon, while two or three would be listed together.However, NAPi has opposed putting multiple nutrients in a single hexagon, saying each nutrient should have a separate warning. It has also sought larger, bolder warnings, with their size linked to the package’s principal display area.NAPi has further called for implementation by July 2027 or earlier, instead of 2028, and questioned the use of “added sugar”, arguing that total sugar should also be considered. It cited an ICMR-NIN communication calling for the 2024 Dietary Guidelines to be applied as an integrated framework, including energy density and total nutrient levels.
Article Summary: Former FSSAI CEO Pawan Kumar Agarwal says he is comfortable with regulator's position. Food Future Foundation filed an intervention application in Supreme Court on September 22. The application seeks to assist the court on the questions it had raised on the design, scientific basis and implementation of the proposed warning system.

Article Title: FSSAI moves to bar use of ‘paneer’ for non-dairy analogues
Article Text:
Representative image

NEW DELHI: Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has proposed restricting the use of the term “paneer” for products not made from milk-derived ingredients, saying the move is aimed at preventing consumers from being misled about a product’s nature and composition.Under the draft Food Safety and Standards (Prohibition and Restrictions on Sales) Amendment Regulations, 2026, products currently licensed or registered under the “Analogue in Dairy Context” category would have to discontinue the use of “paneer” in their nomenclature, labelling and marketing.The proposed amendment specifically defines the restricted category as “paneer made of constituents not derived from milk.”FSSAI has invited objections and suggestions on the draft, which will be considered after 60 days from publication of the notification.The notification was issued on September 22 and published in the Gazette of India on September 23.
Article Summary: The proposed amendment specifically defines the restricted category as “paneer made of constituents not derived from milk’ FSSAI has invited objections and suggestions on the draft, which will be considered after 60 days from publication of the notification.

Article Title: Government expands the list of permitted chemicals for storage in coastal areas
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: In a move that may boost port-adjacent industries by allowing storage of specific chemicals in coastal areas, the govt has expanded the list of petroleum and chemical products permitted for storage in the coastal regulation zone (CRZ) by amending the existing CRZ notification, 2019.The amendment, published by the Union environment ministry on Thursday, now provides for storing 26 petroleum and chemical products in the coastal areas instead of 23 such products permitted earlier. The additional products are linear alkyl benzene, N-paraffin and carbon black feedstock.The list of 23 already permitted products includes crude oil, LPG, kerosene, aviation fuel, high-speed diesel, lubricating oil, CNG, naphtha, acetic acid, methanol, liquefied natural gas and furnace oil, among others.The amendment was notified to accommodate formal representations made by various State Coastal Zone Management Authorities to facilitate the industrial receipt and storage of these specific chemicals in coastal areas. The decision was finally taken after the sectoral Expert Appraisal Committee for CRZ clearances and the National Coastal Zone Management Authority gave their nod.The ministry’s notification said that National Coastal Zone Management Authority, after due deliberation, considering the comparatively lower hazardous chemical characteristics of these products in relation to those already permitted, “unanimously recommended allowing the receipt and storage of Linear Alkyl Benzene, N-Paraffin, and Carbon Black Feedstock in CRZ areas”, excluding Coastal Regulation Zone-IA, through the necessary amendment.It means these products will not be allowed for storage in the environmentally most critical CRZ-IA areas (like mangroves, coral reefs, and turtle nesting grounds) along the coastline. This zone plays a vital role in maintaining the structural integrity of the coast and acting as a natural defence against hazards like cyclones, storms, and tsunamis.
Article Summary: The amendment, published by the Union environment ministry on Thursday, now provides for storing 26 petroleum and chemical products in the coastal areas. The additional products are linear alkyl benzene, N-paraffin and carbon black feedstock. The decision was finally taken after the sectoral Expert Appraisal Committee for CRZ clearances and the National Coastal Zone Management Authority gave their nod.

Article Title: Draft National Electricity Policy moved for inter-ministerial consultation
Article Text:
Electric transmission towers in frame as Power ministry sends draft National Electricity Policy 2026 to Cabinet

NEW DELHI: Union power ministry has finalised the draft National Electricity Policy (NEP) and moved the Cabinet note for inter-ministerial consultation.Released in Jan this year, the draft National Electricity Policy has proposed index-linked automatic annual tariff revision, sought to limit cross-subsidies for the manufacturing sector and railways, increase nuclear capacity, repurpose older thermal units for grid support, and take measures to reduce transmission and distribution losses.Union power secretary Pankaj Agarwal said the ministry received a number of comments and suggestions from stakeholders, which were subsequently examined and accommodated in the draft policy.“We have aggregated all the stakeholders’ comments. We have already moved the Cabinet note for inter-ministerial consultation and I think it shouldn’t be taking very long,” Agarwal told reporters on the sidelines of the 2nd Indian Power Sector Conference organised by Ficci.The last NEP was notified in 2005, when the sector was facing challenges such as demand-supply gaps, limited electricity access and inadequate infrastructure.“Today we are at a very different level...we are already at 300 gigawatt of non-fossil and now going forward, the challenges are entirely different like grid management and building transmission systems,” he said.With the rise in renewable energy, grid stability has emerged as a major challenge, along with under-utilisation of transmission lines during non-solar hours.Agarwal said grid utilisation was also a dimension of NEP 2026. “You can't expect it to be utilised 24x7 at a particular level. There will be more fluctuations. If we can really use 60% of grid capacity, I think that’s a fairly good thing,” he said.The power secretary also said steps were being taken to indigenously design and produce chips for smart meters and the ministry had mandated requirements for their manufacturing, along with timelines. He added that some of the designs had to be tested and validated before commercial production began.
Article Summary: The draft National Electricity Policy has proposed index-linked automatic annual tariff revision. It also sought to limit cross-subsidies for the manufacturing sector and railways. The last NEP was notified in 2005, when the sector was facing challenges such as demand-supply gaps.

NEW DELHI: The Food Safety and Standards Authority of India ( FSSAI ) has proposed restricting the use of the term “paneer” for analogue paneer and cheese products, seeking to prevent consumers from being misled about the nature and composition of the food they buy.The proposed amendment would affect food business operators, including hotels, restaurants and catering services, that use substitutes for traditional dairy-based paneer or cheese products.Under the proposal, products made using paneer or cheese analogues would have to be clearly identified to consumers. The FSSAI said businesses using such products must disclose the information prominently at consumer touchpoints, including menu cards and packaging labels, in line with the Food Safety and Standards (labelling and display) Regulations.The FSSAI notification said: "The amendment is proposed in the following regulation to restrict manufacturing and sale of analogue product as paneer so as to prevent misleading of consumer’s regarding the nature and composition of the product. Products already licensed or registered under ‘Analogue in Dairy Context’ category shall discontinue the use of the term “Paneer” in their nomenclature, labelling or marketing.The proposal also states that products already licensed or registered under the ‘Analogue in Dairy Context’ category would have to discontinue the use of the term “Paneer” in their nomenclature, labelling or marketing.The FSSAI said the proposed changes are aimed at ensuring consumers are not misled about products that are not traditional dairy-based paneer or cheese.The proposal comes amid increased food safety inspections and regulatory scrutiny over the labelling and composition of food products.

Article Text:

9. What’s the row about appointing election commissioners?

10. So, what is the larger question raised by the EC row?

NEW DELHI: Two of three election commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi , formally objected at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions taken in the full Commission's name, according to an Indian Express report.On Wednesday, a Supreme Court-bench was split on the challenge to the law used to appoint them and asked the CJI to set up a five-judge bench.The row lays bare three unsettled questions about election referee: who decides, who controls the voter database, and who picks the people at the top.Here are 10 questions at the centre of the controversy.The objections concern some of the most basic functions of election administration.According to the Express investigation, Sandhu and Joshi raised issues involving changes to Form 6, used by new voters seeking registration; deletion and restoration of names during SIR; appeals against decisions restoring voters; and access to and control over the electoral-roll database. Some notes also questioned communications allegedly issued in the Election Commission's name without approval of the Commission.The EC's response is that these were inputs during decision-making, that differing opinions are natural within a multi-member body, and that final decisions ultimately had the approval of all three commissioners.Absolutely. The law explicitly expects that they sometimes will.Section 18 of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners Act, 2023 says Commission business should, “as far as possible”, be conducted unanimously.“As far as possible” is the key phrase here.But it immediately provides for what happens when unanimity fails: if the CEC and Election Commissioners differ on an issue, the matter is decided according to the majority opinion.With three commissioners, the mathematics is straightforward: 2-1 decides the matter.The more intriguing issue in the current controversy is different: What happens if two commissioners say an action should not have been taken without the approval of the full Commission?The CEC unquestionably has an important institutional position, but the other two commissioners are not deputies who simply report to the chief.This question was fought over dramatically during T N Seshan's tenure. The Supreme Court upheld the creation of a multi-member Election Commission and rejected the idea that the other commissioners were merely ornamental additions. Decisions could legally be taken by majority.The 2023 law reinforces the collegial structure. It says the Commission's procedure and allocation of business may be regulated through a unanimous decision, while disagreements on substantive matters can be resolved by majority.So “Chief” does not mean the CEC has an automatic casting vote over two colleagues.In some respects, the arrangement resembles a three-judge bench more than a conventional government department headed by a secretary.Because the reported disagreement is not simply over what the Commission should decide.Some of the notes reported by the Express raise an important question: Who authorised actions to be taken in the Commission's name in the first place?In April, for example, Sandhu and Joshi separately flagged communications they said had been issued without the requisite approval of the Commission, according to the investigation.The factual question is therefore not merely whether commissioners had different views, but whether the disputed actions fell within areas requiring approval by the Commission and, if so, what approval existed.The EC says its final decisions were collectively and unanimously taken.Yes.Election Commissioner Ashok Lavasa disagreed with the majority in five Model Code of Conduct cases involving complaints against PM Modi and then BJP president Amit Shah. In some cases the Commission's final position was reached 2-1.But the current episode is not identical.The reported notes by Sandhu and Joshi relate heavily to administration of the electoral-roll system and the process by which actions were authorised, rather than commissioners being formally outvoted 2-1.And this time, the two commissioners raising concerns constitute two of the three members.That question remains unresolved politically and institutionally.The case for confidentiality is that collegial bodies need room for frank internal discussion. Officials may become more guarded if every disagreement is immediately made public, particularly while elections are underway.The opposite argument is that disclosure can demonstrate that controversial decisions were debated rather than simply rubber-stamped.This is a practice followed by RBI and SC.At the RBI's Monetary Policy Committee, the law requires publication not only of the final resolution but also how every member voted and each member's written explanation.The Supreme Court routinely publishes majority and dissenting judgments.The Election Commission has traditionally taken a different approach. The present row has therefore revived an old question: Should an institution whose law explicitly provides for majority decisions also have a formal mechanism for publishing minority reasoning?Because election administration is increasingly also software administration.The law places responsibility for constituency electoral rolls with statutory officials such as Electoral Registration Officers. But modern voter rolls are maintained through interconnected digital platforms.The Express investigation reports that Sandhu and Joshi questioned growing centralisation of access to the electoral database and the extent to which local statutory officials retained control. One episode cited involved 97 Goa voters who had been found eligible by electoral officials but could not immediately be restored because the software lacked the required facility at that stage, according to the report.The EC says its digital systems operate with appropriate security safeguards and that statutory election officials retain their legal powers.The simple answer is: Scale.The Election Commission's Special Intensive Revision has involved electoral rolls across multiple states and Union Territories. More than 13 crore names were excluded from draft rolls during the exercise across 30 states and UTs.Exclusion from a draft roll is not necessarily permanent: Voters may make claims, submit documents and pursue appeals.But depriving any electorate from casting vote for any election, howsoever local, should be treated as a serious issue in any democracy. The system needs to find a quick way to rectify it.Delhi SIR exercise has created a peculiar scenario. More than 33 lakh voters have received notices over matters including “logical discrepancies”, prompting the Supreme Court to question whether some notices appeared to have been issued “mechanically” and ask whether additional filters were needed.On September 23, Justices Dipankar Datta and Satish Chandra Sharma differed on selection mechanism of election commissioners. Justice Sharma favoured reference to a five-judge Constitution Bench; Justice Datta took a different view and emphasised that the EC must not only be independent but also appear independent. The matter is now to go before the Chief Justice for constitution of an appropriate bench.It is less about whether disagreement inside the Election Commission is healthy or unhealthy. A three-member constitutional body is designed to accommodate disagreement.The bigger issue is whether there are clear rules for what happens around that disagreement.It’s also about the sanctity of electoral rolls. No eligible voter should be deprived of their right to cast vote in any kind of polls.
Article Summary: Two of three election commissioners, Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi, objected at least 14 times in 10 months to decisions taken in the full Commission's name. Supreme Court-bench was split on the challenge to the law used to appoint them and asked the CJI to set up a five-judge bench.

NEW DELHI: On a day when Election Commission found itself under the scanner, a two-judge bench of Supreme Court gave a split verdict on whether the issue of validity of the law on appointment of CEC/ECs be referred to a constitution bench, but later agreed to refer the case to a larger bench for the sake of early adjudication of the contentious issue.Validity of several provisions of the Chief Election Commissioner and Other Election Commissioners (Appointment, Conditions of Service and Term of Office) Act, 2023 has been challenged on the ground that the law gives the executive "overwhelming" power to appoint its nominee as election commissioner, as the selection panel composed of the PM, a Cabinet minister and the leader of the opposition is designed to give govt a 2:1 majority. The petitioners contended that EC's independence would be compromised in this process.The 2023 law was framed to replace an SC verdict which had directed that selection be done by a committee of the PM, CJI and leader of the opposition until Parliament determined the composition by passing a law. "Speaking in one voice would have better served institutional cohesion. Unfortunately, the court is divided in its opinion," a bench of Justices Dipankar Datta and S C Sharma said.The hearing in the case went on for five days and at the fag end of proceedings, the Centre had sought referral of the case to a constitution bench.Noting that appointment of CEC/ECs was being litigated for last 11 years in SC after a petition was filed in 2015, the bench decided that the case should not be referred to a three-judge bench, which is the normal procedure, but to a constitution bench to settle the issue once and for all. It reasoned that a decision by a three-judge bench would be of little worth and only delay adjudication of the significant issue(s) that these writ petitions raise."Thus, we direct that the papers be placed before the CJI for considering the desirability of constituting a constitution bench of such number of judges to decide the question of vires of Sec 7 and the other provisions of Act," the bench said.The bench expressed hope that the case would be given priority as the issues raised were of "foundational importance to the democratic fabric of the country and its citizenry"."Petitioners seem to be justified in expressing their anxiety that references to five-judge benches remain unresolved for years. If statistics are any guide, none can say with any reasonable degree of certainty when long-pending references will get resolved. Undisputedly, this is an area of grave concern and the inordinate delay in resolution of the references is itself a source of institutional embarrassment which all stakeholders ought to strive to avoid. Self-introspection, indeed, is required," it said."We, thus, take this opportunity of requesting the Chief Justice to also explore the necessity of constituting a permanent five-judge bench to decide pure constitutional issues. This is not something novel that we are saying. It has been opined time and again by responsible citizens and we simply endorse their opinion. Given that resolving constitutional issues is the primary task of judges of this court, that must remain its core priority.Pendency of references for far too long, any period between five and 20 years or more, does not reflect well on the institution. It is time that the institution addresses the issue with the urgency and promptitude it deserves," the bench said.
Article Summary: Two-judge bench of Supreme Court gave a split verdict on whether the issue of validity of the law on appointment of CEC/ECs be referred to a constitution bench. The bench later agreed to refer the case to a larger bench for the sake of early adjudication of the contentious issue.

Article Title: SIR queries raised, but pertained to draft stage; focusing on some notes while ignoring others gives only one part of picture: EC

Focusing on some notes while ignoring others gives only one part of picture: EC

NEW DELHI: Faced with criticism for election commissioners S S Sandhu and Vivek Joshi being cut out of crucial decisions, the Election Commission on Wednesday said the “operational queries, inputs and suggestions” raised over the past 10 months by the two commissioners, including on the special intensive revision (SIR) process, remained limited to the draft stages and were part of the standard administrative practice and decision-making process at the Commission.All decisions taken by the commission in the past one year, including SIR, “are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full commission,” EC asserted in a statement rebutting the contention that the chief election commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar was acting unilaterally.EC was reacting to a report in Indian Express claiming that the two election commissioners had objected to steps taken by the poll panel on 14 occasions over 10 months, including the changes made to Form 6 as part of SIR, restricting field officers’ access to electoral roll databases and even regarding postings and foreign tours involving EC personnel.Sandhu and Joshi even wrote to the Cabinet secretary separately on July 29, complaining about redistribution of work by the senior deputy election commissioner (DEC) in charge of administration EC and the resultant centralisation of decision -making , said the report.In its statement, EC said that differing views and observations are a normal part of deliberation in any institution before a final decision is taken.“Written notes, observations, technical suggestions and internal checks and balances are standard, ongoing practices to ensure transparency, legal compliance and operational rigour." EC said all its actions as well as official orders, decisions and administrative decisions have been in accordance with laws and commission's instructions and carry full legal sanction."Highlighting certain specific internal notes/observations spread over the period of 10 months while overlooking the much larger body of approvals, decisions, instructions and initiatives give only one part of the picture," EC said adding that its decisions, instructions, 40 new initiatives and conduct of polls in six states/UTs in the past one year were all based on unanimous decisions by the commission in the past one year.Sources in EC said the objections were largely raised in written notes sent by the election commissioners to the deputy election commissioners (DECs), in many cases after they had signed on the concerned file following a unanimous decision; including in the cases of changes made to Form 6. The two commissioners, Joshi in May and Sandhu in August, had argued that changes in Form 6 could be carried out only by the government. However, sources maintained, after they along with the CEC unanimously approved the file relating to SIR orders for Bihar (Phase 1) and then a dozen states (Phase 2), which listed the revised Form 6 and the accompanying declaration on citizenship. In fact, by the time Sandhu objected, the Supreme Court had already upheld the validity of SIR as well as the processes followed by EC, sources said.As part of his case against powers getting centralised and CEC not taking his two colleagues in confidence, Sandhu had raised the issue of who had authorised filing of appeals on EC's behalf before the SIR tribunals in West Bengal. Sources, however, told TOI that this was as per the Supreme Court order dated April 1, 2026, particularly para 9 that stated that appeals may be filed by "persons whose names have been excluded from the voters list" or "by the authorities of the ECI, who may be aggrieved by the inclusion of names by the adjudicatory authorities".On the commissioners’ alleged objection to centralisation of the electoral roll database or ERONet/ECINet, allegedly with restricted access to field officers like the electoral registration officers (EROs) to decide on addition of deletion of names, the Commission said digital platforms such as ECINet operate under strict data security protocols to prevent unauthorised tampering, manipulation, etc. "IT security checks and audit controls are standard cybersecurity measures implemented across national databases. Statutory authorities, including EROs and district election officers (DEOs), function as per statutory powers for registration and deletion under law,” said EC. Sources in EC told TOI that while EROs and DEOs may have faced access issues due to system errors on some occasions, they have full access to electors databases and have been deciding on roll updations during SIR.Sources in the Commission did not contest Joshi's claim that agenda and minutes of EC meetings were not being circulated, but said this has been the norm before the present commission assumed office.Responding to the objections to decision of the DEC (Administration) to change the officer in charge of IT division, sources said that powers to decide appointment, recruitment, transfers and postings of officers above the level of section officer and posting and transfer of personal staff of election commissioners and DECs were delegated to DEC (Administration) in 1997.Regarding Joshi's April 16 objection to EC officers being sent on foreign trips without the "commission's" approval, sources said the power in this regard has been with the CEC since long.Reacting to Sandhu's objection that he had learnt of EC's new IT modules, portals etc from the media, sources pointed that both Sandhu and Joshi were present at ECINet's launch on January 22.
Article Summary: Election Commission says objections raised over past 10 months were limited to draft stages. All decisions taken by the commission in the past one year, including SIR, “are an outcome of the unanimous decisions of the full commission,” EC says.

Article Title: Tech executive Shannon Burns, who slept in sauna after forgetting room key on Austria trip, can pursue £76 million from Gitpod; tribunal rejects £1 million cap amid OpenAI acquisition
Article Text:
Shannon Burns can pursue a £76 million compensation claim from Gitpod after a tribunal rejected the company’s bid to cap her claim at £1 million. (Photo: Georgia Bates/Solent News)

Burns was dismissed after Austria work trip

Tribunal found disability discrimination

Gitpod sought to cap the claim at £1 million

OpenAI acquisition could affect Burns’ shares

Burns’ lawyer accuses Gitpod of delaying the case

Compensation hearing is still to come

A senior technology executive who was dismissed after sleeping in a sauna during a work trip has been given the right to pursue a £76 million compensation claim against software company Gitpod, in a case that could result in one of the largest awards in British employment tribunal history.Shannon Burns can formally seek £76,071,992 after the Birmingham Employment Tribunal rejected Gitpod’s application to restrict her potential compensation claim to £1 million. The development was reported by The Independent, which said the proposed payout could surpass the current known record of £4.58 million.Burns was hired by Gitpod in late 2022 as its vice-president of engineering, with an annual salary of £220,000 and a £78,000 bonus. Before joining the company, she had held positions at Silicon Valley firms including Slack and Lyft.In April 2023, she attended a team-building event in Lofer, Austria, where she and other employees, including CEO Johannes Landgraf, consumed alcohol.One evening, Burns was unable to enter her room after forgetting her key. Her ADHD, which she had disclosed to the company, was described during the tribunal proceedings as causing significant forgetfulness and a tendency to lose items.Unable to access her room, she slept in a sauna.Following the trip, Landgraf raised concerns about what he described as her “lack of professional accountability”. Burns was dismissed in June 2023.Burns later argued that her male colleagues had also been drinking during the event but that she was the only one dismissed.In 2025, the Birmingham Employment Tribunal ruled in Burns’ favour on her claims of discrimination arising from disability and failure to make reasonable adjustments. Her separate claim of direct sex discrimination was dismissed. The tribunal ordered that a further hearing would determine compensation.Burns has ADHD and has said that she developed PTSD during the period surrounding her dismissal. She has since left the technology industry and is retraining as a therapist.Her £76 million schedule of loss is based largely on projected future earnings and lost equity. According to the case, Burns argues that she could have continued earning at a high level in the technology sector had she not been dismissed.At the latest hearing, Gitpod asked the tribunal to impose a £1,000 deposit order and effectively prevent Burns from pursuing losses above £1 million.The company described her claim for more than £76 million as “extraordinary” and argued that the calculations in her schedule of loss had “little reasonable prospect of success”.Burns’ lawyers opposed the application, describing it as “oppressive”.Employment Judge Rachel Wedderspoon rejected Gitpod’s application. She noted that Burns had an “exceptionally high pay history” and that her calculations included not only lost salary but also potential losses relating to equity.The judge said the size of the claim was “highly unusual” and potentially more typical of awards sought in the United States. However, she concluded that the tribunal could not determine at this stage that Burns’ valuation had little reasonable prospect of success without expert evidence on employment remuneration and medical matters.The tribunal also ordered Gitpod to disclose information concerning the value of its recent sale to OpenAI.Judge Wedderspoon referred to an acquisition value believed to be $400 million (£302 million). Burns is understood to hold a 0.85 per cent stake in Gitpod.Based on that valuation, the tribunal said her shares could be worth around $3.4 million (£2.6 million), potentially rising to $27.85 million (£21 million) in four years if the $400 million figure proves accurate.OpenAI's acquisition of Gitpod, which was rebranded as Ona, has been subject to regulatory proceedings. Australian competition authorities have confirmed that the proposed acquisition involved OpenAI acquiring 100 per cent of Gitpod, Inc., known as Ona.Tara Grossman, an employment lawyer assisting Burns, described the tribunal decision as a “resounding success” and defended the £76 million calculation.She said Burns had already earned more than £1 million in junior technology roles and that her Gitpod compensation package included both a £220,000 salary and equity that could potentially have become highly valuable.Grossman also accused Gitpod of using aggressive legal tactics to prolong the dispute and put pressure on Burns. She said the company’s attempt to reduce the claim to £1 million was particularly problematic because it was aware of the potential value of Burns’ Gitpod shares following the OpenAI transaction.Those assertions are Burns’ legal team's characterization of the proceedings and have not been established as findings of the tribunal.Despite the latest ruling, Burns has not been awarded £76 million.The tribunal has only ruled that she can pursue the amount claimed, while the final compensation figure will be determined at a separate remedy hearing. That hearing is expected to take place after the conclusion of the ongoing appeal proceedings relating to the earlier tribunal ruling.The tribunal’s 2025 judgment established Burns’ successful disability-related claims but left the question of compensation for a later hearing.If Burns ultimately receives an award close to the amount she is seeking, it would represent an extraordinary figure by British employment tribunal standards. The £76 million figure therefore remains a claim being pursued, rather than a sum already awarded by the tribunal.
Article Summary: Shannon Burns can formally seek £76,071,992 from software company Gitpod. She was dismissed after sleeping in a sauna during a work trip in Austria. Gitpod sought to restrict her potential compensation claim to £1 million. The company described her claim for more than £76 million as 'extraordinary'

Article Title: In 2000, California packed 662,700 shredded waste tires beneath an I-880 on-ramp; they cut foundation stress 40%, saved $477,000, and CalRecycle later reported 22 years without repairs or issues
Article Text:
Representative picture

Solving a foundation nightmare on bay mud

Turning toxic waste piles into civil engineering

Long-term performance and financial returns

Engineers working to upgrade a busy highway junction near San Francisco in 2000 faced a serious technical problem. The ground was made up of about 30 feet of unstable bay mud, a soft type of soil that could sink or crack under the weight of normal road-building materials. To solve the problem, project planners used an unusual method: they buried 662,700 shredded waste tires directly beneath the new highway on-ramp. The site, at the intersection of Interstate 880 and Dixon Landing Road in Milpitas, needed a raised embankment about 26 feet high, 700 feet long, and 50 feet wide to support a southbound connecting ramp. Using normal earth or rock fill would have placed a huge amount of weight on the soft ground. This could have caused the road to settle over time and forced engineers to wait up to a year for the soil to become stable.Instead, the California Department of Transportation and local authorities used tire-derived aggregate instead of traditional fill. The lightweight material is made by shredding old vehicle tyres into large pieces of rubber. According to CalRecycle records, the state agency that oversees recycling and waste management programmes, the method reduced downward pressure on the soft soil by about 40%.It also saved $477,000 compared with other lightweight materials, including specially manufactured commercial aggregate. More than two decades later, state records show that the tyre fill has continued to perform without structural repairs or reported performance problems.The soil around San Francisco Bay has created problems for civil engineers for many years. When heavy structures are built on deep layers of soft, water-filled sediment, the weight of traditional soil embankments slowly pushes the ground down. This can cause uneven roads, cracks in structures, and expensive maintenance. When engineers designed the Dixon Landing Road interchange for Interstate 880, they considered two main ways to prevent the road from settling. The first option was to use thousands of tons of normal fill and wait about 12 months for the soft mud underneath to compress and become stable before paving. The second was to use a specially designed lightweight fill that would put less weight on the ground. Normal mineral soil is much heavier than engineered lightweight materials. A standard earth embankment at the site would have placed a downward load of about 3,750 pounds per square foot on the soft foundation. By using tire-derived aggregate, which weighs about one-third as much as normal soil, engineers reduced that load to 2,250 pounds per square foot. This 40 percent reduction in weight meant construction could continue without waiting for a long period of soil settlement, helping the project stay on schedule.The Interstate 880 project also helped solve an environmental problem that had been growing across California during the late 1990s: huge piles of discarded tires. At the time, California produced about 40 million scrap tires each year. Uncontrolled tire piles often caught fire, sending toxic black smoke into the air and producing dangerous oil runoff that could contaminate groundwater. To get the material needed for the interchange, the former California Integrated Waste Management Board, whose responsibilities were later taken over by CalRecycle, made an agreement with transportation officials to collect and transport the shredded tires. In total, workers used 6,627 tons of shredded rubber in the ramp's foundation. To keep the structure stable and prevent heat from building up inside the fill, workers placed the rubber in two separate layers, each up to 10 feet thick, using normal heavy construction equipment. The two rubber layers were separated by a three-foot layer of low-permeability soil. Heavy geotextile fabric was also placed around the sides to stop nearby soil from entering the spaces between the rubber pieces. The shredded tires remain completely covered by normal road materials and pavement, making them invisible to drivers traveling above.The project did more than prevent the road from becoming uneven. It also produced major savings from the beginning. Other lightweight materials considered during planning, such as processed rock and special mineral aggregates, were expensive to purchase. In its official project summaries, CalRecycle reported that using tire-derived aggregate instead of commercial lightweight aggregate saved about $477,000 in total project costs. The Milpitas on-ramp also gave engineers a real-world example of how shredded tires could be used as lightweight road fill. In a CalRecycle case study, state officials reported that after 22 years of continuous highway traffic, the on-ramp had operated without maintenance problems, ground movement, or structural damage. Research by DingXin Cheng, a civil engineering professor at California State University, Chico, who helped develop technical guidelines for the state agency, found that the layered design used at Interstate 880 provided a useful model for similar infrastructure projects. After the Dixon Landing Road interchange proved successful, transportation agencies across North America began using similar methods for lightweight fill. In California, engineers have since used tire-derived aggregate to stabilize damaged highway slopes, fill spaces behind retaining walls, and reduce vibrations beneath light rail transit lines.
Article Summary: Tire-derived aggregate is made by shredding old vehicle tyres into large pieces of rubber. Project planners buried 662,700 shredded tires directly beneath the new highway on-ramp. The method reduced downward pressure on the soft soil by about 40%. It also saved $477,000 compared with other lightweight materials.

Article Title: 'Dry' Uttarakhand to cut power for up to 15 hours
Article Text:
Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd invoked force majeure, implementing power cuts due to lower hydropower generation





DEHRADUN: In an unprecedented move, Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd (UPCL) invoked force majeure and imposed power cuts ranging from 35 minutes to 15 hours after deficient monsoon rainfall reduced river flows and hydropower generation, widening the gap between electricity demand and supply across the state. Heavy industries in Kumaon and Garhwal faced the longest outages on Sept 21-22, while Haldwani recorded the shortest cut of 35 minutes.UPCL managing director PC Dhyani said Uttarakhand Jal Vidyut Nigam Ltd (UJVNL) was generating substantially less power this Sept than a year earlier. “Last Sept, generation during peak hours was 1,094MW, which has come down to 912MW this year because river flows have declined,” he said, putting the average shortfall at around 170MW.UPCL put Uttarakhand’s current daily power demand at around 53 million units against supply of about 48 million units, leaving a gap that has necessitated scheduled cuts across consumer categories. The daily base load requirement in Uttarakhand is around 2,700MW, of which nearly 1,000MW is supplied by the state-owned hydropower plants, meeting around 50% of the demand. The remaining is sourced from the central grid and power exchanges, which offer power generated from different sources, including hydro, thermal and solar.Supply from the central grid has also fallen. Dhyani said peak-hour allocation dropped from 426MW last Sept to 338MW this year, while two units of THDC Ltd’s hydropower project in Tehri Garhwal remained shut because of technical problems and were expected to return to service within a month. This has affected the supply of around 100MW.Coal-supply disruptions affecting thermal plants elsewhere in the country have further tightened availability on power exchanges. “Even after offering around Rs 10 per unit on the exchange, we are able to secure only about 2% of our demand,” Dhyani said.Since Sept 19, UPCL has staggered outages by consumer category. Heavy industries in Kumaon and Garhwal faced 15-hour cuts on Sept 21-22, rural Kumaon around 2 hours 40 minutes, and rural Garhwal about three hours, while Haldwani saw cuts of about 35 minutes.With festive-season demand and Haridwar Ardh Kumbh ahead, UPCL has sought additional supply from the central grid — 100MW in Oct, 150MW in Nov, 300MW in Dec, 400MW in Jan, 300MW in Feb and 175MW in March. It has also restarted a gas-based power plant that will supply around 90MW.Dhyani said field units had been asked to postpone maintenance or carry it out during scheduled outages so consumers did not face additional disruption.
Article Summary: Uttarakhand Power Corporation Ltd imposed power cuts ranging from 35 minutes to 15 hours. deficient monsoon rainfall reduced river flows and hydropower generation. Heavy industries in Kumaon and Garhwal faced the longest outages on Sept 21-22. Haldwani recorded the shortest cut of 35 minutes.

Article Title: Chhagan Bhujbal discharged in Kalina land scam case, last one pending against him
Article Text:
A special court discharged state minister Chhagan Bhujbal and three others in the 2015 Kalina land scam case (File Photo)





MUMBAI: Holding that the prosecution failed to establish a “meeting of minds” or any specific overt act connecting state minister Chhagan Bhujbal to the alleged conspiracy of manipulating a public project to secure kickbacks from a private developer, a special court on Thursday discharged the 74-year-old NCP politician and three others in the 2015 Kalina land scam case.The court concluded there is no evidence Bhujbal instructed his subordinates to manipulate project calculations, alter tender rules or suppress conditions and noted that holding the position of department head does not automatically prove he instigated or aided the alleged offences.The prosecution had accused Bhujbal and others of causing a loss of Rs 79.2 crore to the state govt while processing the Kalina library project on a build-operate-transfer basis and of favouring India Bulls Real Estate Ltd. It was further alleged that eventual award of project to India Bulls Real Estate Ltd was followed by a Rs 2.5 crore sponsorship routed through Indiabulls Realtech Ltd to the Chhagan Bhujbal Welfare Foundation, Nashik, with which Bhujbal was associated.This was the last case pending against Bhujbal before the special court after he was previously granted relief in proceedings related to allegations of kickbacks and siphoning of funds linked to construction of Maharashtra Sadan in Delhi and a housing project in Navi Mumbai.“The applicant’s (Bhujbal) position as PWD minister (then) explains his presence in the governmental process; it does not, by itself, establish his participation in a criminal conspiracy,” special judge Mahesh K Jadhav said.In his 70-page order on Bhujbal’s discharge plea, the judge further said there is no material shown that the land or alleged property was entrusted to Bhujbal in his personal capacity or that he misappropriated or converted it for his own use. The material “reveals that the prosecution has not been able to demonstrate the necessary nexus between the applicant’s official acts and the alleged criminal object,” the judge said.The court noted the project proposal was sanctioned during a committee meeting on Feb 25, 2010, following the (then) CM’s approval and a review of departmental reports, including remarks from the finance department and explanations from the public works department. This decision was taken collectively, with Bhujbal, also deputy CM then, participating as one member of a committee that included then CM Ashok Chavan and cabinet ministers Sunil Tatkare, Ajit Pawar, Rajendra Darda, Shivajirao Moghe, Radhakrishna Vikhe-Patil and Jaydutt Kshirsagar, along with several senior bureaucrats.The judge cleared Bhujbal of all charges under the Prevention of Corruption Act and Indian Penal Code.The court said a minister may convene meetings, call for files, seek progress of a govt project, transfer a project from one office to another and participate in collective governmental decision-making. “Such acts become criminal only when the material demonstrates that they were performed pursuant to a dishonest or illegal design,” the judge said. The court noted the material did not show the “common criminal design” alleged by prosecution.“The committee’s collective decision, even if subsequently alleged to have been based on incorrect technical calculations, cannot automatically be converted into cheating by a minister who was one participant in the governmental process,” the judge said.The court refuted the arguments that subordinate engineers manipulated project calculations under the minister’s “invisible support”. “The prosecution’s mere assumption that this could not be done by the officers without “invisible support” of accused no 1 (Bhujbal) is not sufficient… The court has therefore examined whether the chargesheet contains any direction, communication, meeting, message, financial transaction or other material showing that applicant (Bhujbal) instructed the concerned officers to prepare the report in a particular manner or to manipulate the figures for the benefit of proposed developer. No such specific material has been pointed out,” the judge said.On sponsorship routed to the Chhagan Bhujbal Welfare Foundation, the court said prosecution had to establish a nexus between the official act and alleged pecuniary advantage. The court noted the foundation was registered, had charitable objects, received sponsorships through banking channels and had audited accounts.“There is no statement of any officer of the donor company saying that the sponsorship was demanded by applicant (Bhujbal) in consideration of the library contract. There is no communication from applicant asking for sponsorship. There is no document showing that the amount was negotiated with reference to the value or benefit of the library project,” the judge said.The court held chronological proximity between award of tender and sponsorship was not enough. “In the present material, that additional link is missing,” the judge said.The others discharged are Harish Patil (executive engineer), now retired, Gajanan Sawant (divisional deputy engineer), now retired, and Ravindra Sawant as the private CA allegedly hired to facilitate tender eligibility for India Bulls. Maniklal Shah (secretary, construction) died during pendency of case.Two others, Anilkumar Gaikwad, then PWD superintending engineer and Sanjay Solanki, then PWD undersecretary, were discharged from the case in Feb 2021.The judge stated the tender process did not support the prosecution’s case. The judge said 11 developers purchased tender documents, four submitted offers, two were found eligible, and India Bulls Real Estate Ltd emerged as the highest bidder with an offer of Rs 1.06 crore. The court said no material showed Bhujbal selected the developer, communicated with developer about the tender, or instructed officers to change eligibility criteria in its favour.Bhujbal’s lawyer Sudarshan Khawase argued the BOT concept had originated in departments other than PWD before Bhujbal’s alleged involvement. The prosecution opposed the discharge.
Article Summary: A special court discharged state minister Chhagan Bhujbal and three others in the 2015 Kalina land scam case. The prosecution had accused the 74-year-old NCP politician of causing a loss of Rs 79.2 crore to the state govt.

Article Title: Intel cuts VP ranks from 450 to 200, CFO David Zinsner calls it a 'cultural problem'; says it contributed to products going through four or five...
Article Text:
Intel's leadership was hearing a different story from the one on the ground

Intel says 18A yields and 14A progress show the overhaul is working

Intel has cut the number of vice presidents at the company from about 450 at its peak to roughly 200. It has also halved its management layers from 12 to six as CEO Lip-Bu Tan tries to get the chipmaker to decide faster and ship on time. CFO David Zinsner shared the numbers at the Deutsche Bank Technology Conference, describing the old structure as a cultural problem that hurt Intel's execution for more than a decade.Zinsner said too many people across the organisation held veto power, so decisions kept stalling. The damage showed up in products. Chips often needed four or five development cycles before they were ready, when they should have reached production after the first attempt. Looking back at the last decade, he said much of Intel's trouble "can be boiled down to culture," adding that 50-person startups were getting products out faster than Intel.Transparency was the other big issue. According to Zinsner, information changed as it moved up the management chain, and by the time presentations reached the CEO, they often described a different situation from the one teams lower down knew about.He did not frame this as deliberate deception. Some managers simply did not want to admit a project was failing. The result was that Intel's top leadership sometimes made decisions based on an inaccurate picture of the business. Tan has since brought in executives he trusts who are used to working in leaner organisations.The VP cuts sit inside a much larger downsizing. Intel had 108,900 employees at the end of 2024 and 88,400 by late September 2025, including subsidiaries like Mobileye. Around 20,500 of those exits happened under Tan, who took charge in March 2025 and told staff there would be "no more blank checks." The pitch was about flattening management, but in Oregon only 8% of the laid-off employees had "manager" in their job titles. Most were engineers and technicians.Zinsner pointed to early signs of change. Several products have reached A-stepping, Intel's term for the first version of a chip, without the repeated development cycles that were once routine. Intel 18A yields are running ahead of internal milestones, and 14A defect density is tracking better than the company's target curve.Intel is now preparing for 14A risk production in 2027 and high-volume manufacturing in 2028. Internal product teams have started designing for the process, and interest from external foundry customers has picked up.Finances are moving too. Intel entered 2026 expecting gross margins in the high 30s and is now in the low 40s. The target is the mid-40s, then the high 40s, and eventually a figure starting with 5. To get there, Intel uses an internal "Rule of 45" that combines revenue growth and operating margin. Slower businesses must deliver stronger margins, while faster-growing ones can earn more investment.Halving the VP ranks gives Intel a leaner org chart, but the numbers Zinsner shared will only mean something if they hold. 14A is the first major process being developed entirely under Tan's structure, with fewer layers between engineers and the CEO and fewer people who can block a decision. If it reaches risk production in 2027 and volume manufacturing in 2028 as planned, it will be the clearest evidence yet that the cultural reset worked. If it slips into the multiple development cycles that marked the last decade, the 250 fewer vice presidents will have changed very little.
Article Summary: Intel has cut the number of vice presidents at the company from about 450 at its peak to roughly 200. It has also halved its management layers from 12 to six as CEO Lip-Bu Tan tries to get the chipmaker to decide faster and ship on time.Intel says 18A yields and 14A progress show the overhaul is working.

Article Title: Microsoft shakes up communications team; CEO Satya Nadella and President Brad Smith sends memo to employees, says 'We will likely have more employees and executives acting as ...'
Article Text:
Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described the communications shake-up as a response to a media environment

Why is Microsoft changing its communications strategy

Microsoft communications team will now report to Brad Smith

What happens to Microsoft communications chief Frank Shaw

Microsoft is changing how it communicates with the outside world. The company is moving its communications team out of its marketing organisation and into the corporate, external and legal affairs group led by Vice Chair and President Brad Smith, according to internal memos from Smith and CEO Satya Nadella . The bigger change, however, may be how Microsoft employees speak for the company. Nadella said the company wants engineers, sellers, partners and other employees who are close to its products and customers to play a bigger role in telling Microsoft's story.“We will likely have more employees and executives acting as part of Microsoft’s public voice, including on social media,” Smith wrote in his memo.Microsoft CEO Satya Nadella described the communications shake-up as a response to a media environment that has become “increasingly fragmented and noisier than ever.” Instead of relying mainly on a central communications team to shape Microsoft's public messaging, the CEO wants people closer to the company's work to have a greater role.“In many ways, the people closest to the work have the best opportunity to shape how Microsoft is understood,” Nadella wrote. He said Microsoft wants engineers, sellers, partners and others “closest to our products and customers” to become “an even bigger part of how we tell our story, all connected by a shared strategy and set of principles.”Nadella added: “We will learn, we will experiment, and we will evolve. There is a fundamentally new way to think about communications, and this team will be central to building it.”Under the new structure, Microsoft's communications function will sit within the organisation led by President Brad Smith rather than under marketing. Smith's organisation handles Microsoft's legal, regulatory and public policy work, including antitrust matters, litigation and government relations.The communications team will therefore sit alongside these functions, although Microsoft plans to continue coordination between communications and marketing.Satya Nadella described Smith as one of the few Microsoft leaders who “embody Microsoft’s voice” authentically. He also praised Smith's “rare ability to communicate complex ideas with clarity, conviction, and trust.”The restructuring also changes the role of longtime Microsoft communications chief Frank X. Shaw. Shaw announced earlier this month that he would leave Microsoft at the end of the year after more than two decades with the company. He will now step away from his current responsibilities and serve as an adviser to Smith and interim communications leader Brent Colburn during the transition.Microsoft said Shaw will remain with the company through the end of the year. Shaw described the latest development as the formalisation of the plan that had already been announced.Microsoft said Shaw “has been a trusted counselor and leader at Microsoft for more than two decades, and we’re grateful he will continue to act as an advisor during the transition.”Satya Nadella also thanked Shaw for his contribution. He said Shaw has “made tremendous contributions to the company and to our communications function over the last 17+ years” and has been “a great source of counsel to our leadership team and to me personally, across the company’s biggest moments.”Smith also praised Shaw, saying he had “worked as closely with him as almost anyone” over the years. Smith added that Shaw's “enduring impact on Microsoft and this team will be felt for years to come. I will miss him.”
Article Summary: Microsoft is moving its communications team out of its marketing organisation and into the corporate, external and legal affairs group led by Vice Chair and President Brad Smith. The bigger change, however, may be how Microsoft employees speak for the company. Nadella said the company wants engineers, sellers, partners and other employees who are close to its products and customers to play a bigger role.
