Article Title: Budget phones are disappearing fast, report says by 2030, 40% of sub-Rs 20,000 smartphones may be gone
Article Text:
Why budget phones’ shipment will squeeze

Smartphone shipment rebound expected through 2030

The era of the budget smartphones is rapidly shrinking. Over 230 million annual smartphone shipments priced below $200 (Rs 20,000) will vanish from worldwide retail channels between 2025 and 2030, a report has said. According to Counterpoint Research’s Smartphone Shipment Forecast by Price Band tracker, this segment will contract by roughly 40% through the end of the decade. The decline comes even as total worldwide smartphone shipments stage a broader rebound back toward 2025 volumes.The disappearing budget tier stems largely from structural aftershocks linked to the 2026–2027 industry downturn. A combination of rising prices for mobile chipsets and memory, higher baseline hardware requirements and phone makers scaling back unprofitable market footprints has made entry-level devices increasingly hard to sustain, the report said, adding, as components eat up a far larger share of total build costs on inexpensive devices, manufacturers have virtually no room to absorb price jumps.It also said that rather than buying brand-new budget handsets, consumers are responding in several ways. For example, users are delaying upgrades and extending how long they keep their existing devices. Some buyers are turning to certified refurbished and second-hand phones, and a portion of buyers is moving up into higher price tiers via installment plans.“The smartphone market will recover in unit terms, but the affordable segment will not return to its previous standing.The opportunity now shifts toward better-specced mainstream devices and premium products, although higher tiers cannot absorb all the lost volume. The result will be a market that is similar in overall size but materially different in value and competitive profile. There is also a wider connectivity risk, as the loss of affordable new smartphones could make it harder for first-time users in lower-income markets to come online,” said Yang Wang, Principal Analyst at Counterpoint Research.Counterpoint estimates that overall smartphone deliveries will climb back to approximately 1.20 billion units by 2030, just behind 2025 benchmark levels. The stagnation across the mid-range highlights that budget volume is not simply flowing upward in a straight line. Instead, delayed purchase cycles and disappearing first-time buyer demand mean higher tiers will not make up for all the lost volume under $200.Across developing and lower-income markets, device affordability remains the single greatest roadblock to mobile internet access. As sub-$200 options disappear, the transition from basic feature phones or shared family devices to personal smartphone ownership risks slowing to a crawl. This slowdown threatens to complicate long-term efforts by network operators, software developers, and governments seeking to broaden digital public infrastructure, localized content and mobile financial services.
Article Summary: Over 230 million annual smartphone shipments priced below $200 (Rs 20,000) will vanish from worldwide retail channels between 2025 and 2030. The disappearing budget tier stems largely from structural aftershocks linked to the 2026–2027 industry downturn. Counterpoint estimates that overall smartphone deliveries will climb back to approximately 1.20 billion units by 2030.

Article Title: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic may launch AI safety standard by early 2027
Article Text:
Momentum builds following safety proposals

Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are said to be collaborating to establish an independent artificial intelligence (AI) safety body by late 2026 or early 2027, a report from The Information has claimed, adding that they have reached out to former White House AI policy advisor Sriram Krishnan to serve as chief executive. The report says that the planned organisation, provisionally named the Standards Authority for Frontier AI (SAFA), will operate independently of government administration. Its primary mission will be to define practical benchmarks for the three companies' public safety pledges and provide direct support to developers evaluating cutting-edge models prior to commercial deployment.Citing people familiar with the initiative, the report said that apart from Krishnan, the companies have reached out to Arati Prabhakar, former director of the White House Office of Science and Technology Policy, to take the top post at SAFA. The three technology giants are also weighing whether SAFA should conduct direct model assessments in-house.While the United States Center for AI Standards and Innovation already handles federal evaluation, insiders noted persistent concerns that the government agency lacks adequate technical and financial resources to thoroughly inspect complex frontier systems.The push toward a joint authority follows weeks of escalating industry dialogue.About 10 days ago, an OpenAI spokesperson confirmed to CNBC that the company was holding active talks with Google and Anthropic regarding coordinated safety frameworks. These discussions gained momentum following a proposal published on X in July by Sir Demis Hassabis, co-founder of Google DeepMind and Alphabet’s chief scientist. Hassabis argued for a US-backed standards body modeled after a public-private partnership or a self-regulatory watchdog, drawing comparisons to the Financial Industry Regulatory Authority (FINRA).While Google, Anthropic, and OpenAI remain locked in a race for commercial dominance, leadership across all three firms has faced mounting scrutiny over potential catastrophic and security risks. The momentum toward collective oversight accelerated earlier this month after Anthropic CEO Dario Amodei released an essay calling for an industrywide slowdown in the release of frontier models to allow safety mechanisms to catch up.
Article Summary: Google, OpenAI and Anthropic are said to be collaborating to establish an independent artificial intelligence (AI) safety body by late 2026 or early 2027. The planned organisation, provisionally named the Standards Authority for Frontier AI (SAFA), will operate independently of government administration. Its primary mission will be to define practical benchmarks for the three companies' public safety pledges.

Article Title: Vodafone Idea introduces free international roaming across 170+ countries
Article Text:
Here’s what Vi’s new free international roaming plan covers

Telecom operator Vodafone Idea has announced a new proposition that offers free international roaming across postpaid, prepaid, and enterprise plans. The move, part of its brand promise “Vi Pe Sab Hain VIP”, allows customers and their families to stay connected in over 170 countries without worrying about roaming charges, SIM swaps, or unexpected bills.Under the new proposition, eligible customers can enjoy free international roaming bundled into their plans:•Postpaid plans starting at Rs 501•Annual prepaid unlimited data plans•Enterprise plans starting at Rs 451Depending on the plan, users can access free roaming benefits for up to three trips per year, with varying international data quotas and outgoing minutes. Vi estimates that customers could save up to ₹9,000 annually. Activation is simple via the Vi App, where users can select the “Roam-Free” option before travel.Coverage across countries•170+ countries included in the roaming benefit.•Customers can use their Indian number abroad without needing local SIMs or travel eSIMs.Benefits included•Free international roaming for up to three trips per year, depending on the plan.•Varying international data quotas and outgoing call minutes bundled in.•Estimated savings of up to Rs 9,000 annually for frequent travellers.Convenience and security•Seamless access to OTPs, calls, and data abroad.•Avoid reliance on unsecured public Wi-Fi.•Easy activation via the Vi App with “Roam-Free” option.Avneesh Khosla, Chief Marketing Officer at Vi, said “Traditionally, international roaming has been perceived as expensive. We are taking a disruptive approach by making it a built-in benefit. Your Vi number now travels with you for free. This is exactly what ‘Vi Pe Sab Hain VIP’ stands for — solving real customer pain points with meaningful benefits.”
Article Summary: Vodafone Idea has announced a new proposition that offers free international roaming across postpaid, prepaid, and enterprise plans. The move, part of its brand promise ‘Vi Pe Sab Hain VIP’, allows customers and their families to stay connected in over 170 countries.

Article Title: McDonald's says its AI-enabled drive-thru system can now take orders in English and Spanish with 90% accuracy; it could save at least 50 labour hours a week; CFO Ian Borden notes that company has no i
Article Text:
$8.5 billion global modernization plan of McDonald’s

Archy and ArchIQ: AI at the center of the plan

Beyond AI: physical store upgrades

Menu changes driven by protein demand

Staying focused on value amid cost-of-living pressure

Employee training and customer value

McDonald’s announced that its AI-enabled drive-thru system called Archy can now take orders in both English and Spanish with 90% accuracy. According to a report by CBS, the company said that the system could save at least 50 labour hours per week at a typical restaurant by streamlining order-taking. CFO Ian Borden also stressed that the intention is not to reduce staff but to free employees to focus on hospitality and food preparation tasks, such as hand-breading chicken.The announcement came as McDonald’s unveiled a $8.5 billion investment plan over the next decade to modernize its 46,000 restaurants worldwide. CEO Chris Kempczinski said the company must improve productivity and capture market share in a flat fast-food traffic environment. Planned upgrades include lockers for delivery orders, redesigned kitchen layouts, bigger play areas, and more visible coffee preparation stations to enhance quality perceptions.A key piece of the modernization push is McDonald's AI-enabled drive-thru ordering system, Archy, which the company says can now take orders in both English and Spanish with 90% accuracy. According to CFO Ian Borden, the system could eventually save at least 50 labor hours per week at a typical restaurant.Importantly, Borden was clear that the goal isn't to cut staffing — instead, employees freed up from order-taking would be redirected toward hospitality-focused tasks or hands-on food preparation work, like hand-breading chicken.Archy operates alongside ArchIQ, a broader AI system McDonald's developed in partnership with Google that's designed to improve order accuracy while automating backend tasks like inventory management and staff scheduling. Kempczinski said early testing shows customers have responded well to Archy specifically because it makes their orders more accurate, adding that the company's approach to AI isn't rooted in treating the technology as inherently good or bad, but in being deliberate about how it's actually deployed.The modernization plan extends well past software. McDonald's said upcoming restaurant redesigns will include lockers for handling delivery orders, more visible coffee preparation areas meant to improve customers' perception of quality, larger play areas, and reworked kitchen layouts. Order-accuracy scales, already active in 10,000 restaurants globally, are set to expand to 20,000 locations by 2028.On the food side, McDonald's highlighted strong results from its hand-breaded chicken, currently rolled out across 10,000 restaurants in Asia and a small number of locations near Chicago, with plans to expand testing into additional US markets and Ireland next year — a category where rivals like Chick-fil-A and KFC have long had an edge. The company also plans to introduce grilled chicken sandwiches and wraps, along with experimenting with items like egg bites and bowls.Skye Anderson, president of McDonald's USA, tied this shift directly to changing consumer habits, noting that roughly 30 million Americans currently use GLP-1 weight loss drugs and are increasingly seeking smaller, protein-dense meals as a result. She pointed to internal research suggesting a much larger opportunity, though, with roughly 60 million Americans actively looking to add more protein to their diets overall — a gap she framed as a chance for McDonald's to give customers more reasons to choose the brand first.Despite the modernization push, Kempczinski emphasized that value remains central to McDonald's strategy, particularly for lower-income consumers. He defined low-income US households as those earning $45,000 or less annually, noting that while this group still eats fast food, they're doing so less frequently than before. He credited meal bundles like the $5 meal deal with helping address that pressure, and said McDonald's is exploring introducing entry-level pricing on a basic menu of items in the US, mirroring an approach it already uses in Europe and other markets. He described the current economic backdrop as one demanding constant attention to value, noting that cost-of-living pressure on consumers isn't going away anytime soon.McDonald’s is also rolling out new hospitality-focused training, showing employees what a perfectly cooked Big Mac tastes like and encouraging more pleasant customer interactions. At the same time, the company remains focused on value, exploring entry-level pricing for basic menu items in the U.S. to counter cost-of-living pressures.
Article Summary: McDonald’s announced that its AI-enabled drive-thru system called Archy can now take orders in both English and Spanish with 90% accuracy. The company said that the system could save at least 50 labour hours per week at a typical restaurant by streamlining order-taking. CFO Ian Borden stressed that the intention is not to reduce staff but to free employees to focus on hospitality and food preparation tasks, such as hand-breading chicken.
